newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Commission review of aid to Vulcan inadequate.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Commission review of aid to Vulcan inadequate.

text.p: The European Court of Justice annulled on Thursday the Commission's characterisation of state aid to Hibeg, and subsequently to Bremer Vulkan, as illegal.
When Bremer Vulkan (BV) purchased Krupps Atlas Elektronik (KAE), the consideration provided to Krupp consisted of 2.8 million shares in BV, valued at DM 350 million.

Later, after a series of transactions, those same shares were valued at only 80 percent of the original value, or DM 224 million. The German state of Bremen provided a bank guarantee for the difference between the two values, allowing the sale between BV and KAE to take place.
The Commission found the guarantee amounted to illegal state aid because Hibeg was wholly owned by the state of Bremen and should be considered a public undertaking.

The court reasoned that the question of illegal state aid hinged in part on whether the total value of the BV shares amounted to the 75 percent share capital of KAE which BV acquired, or whether the amount was less.
The court found the Commission's statement of reasons for deciding the aid was illegal was inadequate.

"The Commission merely stated, without adequate explanation, that the stock price is the sole determining factor in valuing shares. That view is too formal, rigid and restrictive. To apply that criterion absolutely and unconditionally, to the exclusion of all other elements, constitutes a purely mechanical exercise which can scarely be reconciled with the system of the market economy and the economic choices made in the present case by undertakings of substantial size guided by prospects of profitablity in the longer term," the court said.

"State aid - Guarantee given by the public authorities in favour indirectly of a shipbuilding undertaking for the acquisition of an undertaking in another sector - Diversification of the activities of the recipient undertaking - Recovery"
In Joined Cases C-329/C-62/95 and C-63/95
Federal Republic of Germany
and

and
Bremer Vulkan Verbund AG, applicants
v
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

application for annulment of Commission decision 94/412/EEC of 6 April 1993 concerning aid awarded by the German government to Hibeg via Krupp GmbH to Bremer Vulkan AG, facilitating the sale of Krupp Atlas Elektronik GmbH from Krupp GmbH to Bremer Vulkan AG (OJ 1993 L 185, p. 43)
THE COURT hereby

1. Annuls Commission decision 94/412/EEC of 6 April 1993 concerning aid awarded by the German government to Hibeg via Krupp GmbH to Bremer Vulkan AG, facilitating the sale of Krupp Atlas Elektronik GmbH from Krupp GmbH to Bremer Vulkan AG;
2. Orders the Commission of the European Communities to pay the costs.
